examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: An activation record is created for each dynamic call and stores information such as return address, saved context and local data. Recursive calls have distinct automatic locals; static data is shared across activations. Activation trees preserve nesting and call order; tail-call optimization is a separate implementation choice.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
main calls f once; f calls g twice sequentially. Counting main, what is the maximum number of simultaneously active calls?

**Answer: 3.** At either g call the live chain is main→f→g, containing three activations. The two g invocations do not overlap. The activation tree has four total nodes but maximum depth three.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Total call count differs from peak stack depth. Dynamic links record callers; static/access links support lexical nesting and may point elsewhere.

The caller relationship and lexical nesting relationship are different.
